system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- Evidence text comes from a PDF text layer. If symbols are garbled so that you cannot verify the atom, answer "hold" for that check and say so.
- Be strict. When unsure between pass and a non-pass value, choose the non-pass value and explain.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom. pass = fully stated. revise = the core claim is stated, and the gap is only wording, strength, or a dropped/extra peripheral qualifier that can be fixed by deleting or softening words (say what). fail = not stated, OR the atom adds substantive content the evidence lacks: a scope or population restriction (e.g. 'In B-ALL'), a mechanism or operation, a characterization (e.g. 'an unbounded while loop'), or a formula/definition. If deleting the unsupported part would change what the atom tests, it is fail, not revise. For pass, put the supporting evidence ids in cite (required).
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / revise / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge: one fact a person who studied the concept would simply know. revise = the core fact is recall-level but the sentence carries extra load that must be removed, e.g. stacked conditions (since/although/if ... and ...), a procedural or evaluative add-on ('easy to define but requires checking ...'), or a clause that introduces a second technical concept that must be known separately (e.g. 'if X is an inner Kan complex' when that is not the card concept). fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = the authors' opinion or choice, or the finding of one study, so the answer is not fixed without the source.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a single system, product, or one study's topic.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}

CONCEPT: Boardman–Vogt resolution
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: The W-construction for operads: trees with edge lengths, relations for length-0 edges and unit vertices, W(P)→P, algebras up to coherent homotopy, and the simplicial version with ∆[1]. Excludes the later homotopy-coherent nerve comparison.

ATOMS:
- HMDEND-C02-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: For an operad $P$, the Boardman–Vogt resolution is an operad $W(P)$ with the same set of colours as $P$, together with a map of operads $\varepsilon: W(P)\to P$ that is the identity on colours.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0047-s02] For an operad P, we will present a ‘resolution’ by a map of operads
    [HMDEND-p0047-s03] The new operad W(P) has the same set of colours as P and the map ε is the identity on colours.
- HMDEND-C02-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: An operation of $W(P)(c_1,\dots,c_n;c)$ is represented by a tree with leaves labelled $c_1,\dots,c_n$, root labelled $c$, edges labelled by colours, vertices labelled by operations of $P$, and in addition every edge given a length in $[0,1]$ such that the external edges (leaves and root) all have length 1.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0048-s17] For its construction, recall that elements in FU(P)(c1, . . ., cn; c) are represented by trees T with leaves labelled by the set {c1, . . ., cn} and root by c.
    [HMDEND-p0048-s18] The edges of T are labelled by colours in C and the vertices of T are labelled by operations of P. Two such labelled trees represent the same point in FU(P)(c1, . . ., cn; c) if they are related by an isomorphism of trees respecting colours and operations in the way explained in Section 1.5.
    [HMDEND-p0048-s21] W(P)(c1, . . ., cn; c) are represented by labelled trees as for FU(P), where in addition the edges are all given a length t ∈[0, 1] ⊆R.
    [HMDEND-p0048-s22] This assignment of lengths must be such that the external edges of T, i.e. the leaves and the root, all have length 1.
- HMDEND-C02-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: The idea is that $W(P)$-algebras are 'P-algebras up to coherent homotopy', and $W(P)$ is a topological operad even when $P$ itself is discrete.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0047-s06] The idea is that W(P)-algebras are ‘P-algebras up to coherent homotopy’.
    [HMDEND-p0047-s07] This operad W(P) will be a topological operad, also when P itself is discrete.
- HMDEND-C02-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: The equivalence relation on length-labelled trees defining $W(P)$ is generated by three kinds of identification: isomorphisms of trees respecting labellings (including lengths), contraction of edges of length zero, and erasure of vertices labelled by a unit operation.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0050-s04] To summarize, operations of W(P) are represented by trees whose edges have
    [HMDEND-p0050-s05] a colour and a length and whose vertices are labelled by operations of P. The equivalence relation on such representatives is generated by identifications of three kinds:
    [HMDEND-p0050-s06] (i) one related to isomorphisms of trees, respecting the labellings,
    [HMDEND-p0050-s07] (ii) one related to edges of length zero,
    [HMDEND-p0050-s08] (iii) one related to vertices labelled by a unit.
- HMDEND-C02-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: In $W(P)$, a labelled tree with an inner edge of length zero is identified with the smaller tree obtained by contracting that edge and labelling the newly arising vertex by the appropriate composition in $P$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0049-s03] If an edge has length zero, then the operation in W(P) represented by that labelled tree is to be identified with the one represented by the smaller labelled tree obtained by contracting the edge of length zero and labelling the newly arising vertex by the appropriate composition in P. Let us illustrate this relation by an example.
- HMDEND-C02-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: In $W(P)$, a vertex labelled by a unit operation is erased, and the newly arising edge is given as length the maximum of the lengths of the two edges that were attached to that vertex.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0049-s07] The other relation identifies a labelled tree where a vertex v is labelled by a unit
    [HMDEND-p0049-s08] operation of P with the smaller labelled tree obtained by ‘erasing’ that vertex and giving the newly arising edge as its length the maximum of the lengths of the two edges connected to v.
- HMDEND-C02-S2-04 | S2
  ATOM: In $W(P)$, a tree having a vertex labelled by a unit operation is identified with the tree obtained by erasing that vertex, where the new merged edge is given length equal to the maximum of the lengths of the two edges that met at that vertex.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0049-s07] The other relation identifies a labelled tree where a vertex v is labelled by a unit
    [HMDEND-p0049-s08] operation of P with the smaller labelled tree obtained by ‘erasing’ that vertex and giving the newly arising edge as its length the maximum of the lengths of the two edges connected to v.
    [HMDEND-p0050-s01] Here the new length u is the maximum of s and t.
- HMDEND-C02-S2-05 | S2
  ATOM: Composition in $W(P)$ is defined by grafting trees, identifying a leaf of one tree with the root of another (both have the same colour and length 1) and carrying along all labels, so compositions of subtree operations can be recognized by edges of length 1.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0051-s05] sends operations represented by trees T, S1, . . ., Sn to the operation represented by identifying the ith leaf of T with the root of Si and carrying along all the labels.
    [HMDEND-p0051-s06] Note that this ith leaf has the same colour as the root of Si, as well as the same length (namely 1).
    [HMDEND-p0051-s07] Thus, one can recognize operations in W(P) that arise as a composition of operations represented by subtrees by looking for edges of length 1.
- HMDEND-C02-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: For a simplicial operad $P$, the simplicial Boardman–Vogt resolution is built analogously to the topological one by replacing the topological unit interval with the simplex $\Delta[1]$, giving a simplicial operad $WP$ with a map to $P$ that is the identity on colours.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0107-s02] For a simplicial operad P, one can mimic the topological Boardman–Vogt resolution for topological operads (as in Section 1.7) and construct a simplicial operad WP equipped with a map to P which is the identity on colours.
    [HMDEND-p0107-s03] The modification to the simplicial case is done completely analogously to the W-construction for simplicial categories of Section 2.7.3, replacing the topological unit interval by the simplex ∆[1].
- HMDEND-C02-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: For a category $C$ viewed as an operad with only unary operations, a $W(C)$-algebra $A$ is not a functor on $C$ itself: it respects identities, but respects composition only up to homotopy, since $A_t(f_2,f_1)$ is a homotopy between $A(f_2f_1)$ and $A(f_2)\circ A(f_1)$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0052-s14] Thus, the At( f2, f1) provide a homotopy between A( f2 f1) and the composition A( f2)◦
    [HMDEND-p0052-s15] A( f1). This shows that A is not a functor on C itself: it respects identities, but it
    [HMDEND-p0052-s16] respects composition only up to homotopy.
- HMDEND-C02-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: The operad $W(P)$ is a topological operad even when $P$ itself is discrete.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0047-s07] This operad W(P) will be a topological operad, also when P itself is discrete.
